Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:
  • Acute gastroenteritis – watery diarrhea 5–6×/day for 3 days, initial vomiting (resolved), possible dehydration, weakness.  
  • Past history: asthma (uses blue reliever inhaler PRN).  
- Relevant family medical history:
  • Father – hypertension; died of bowel cancer ~10 yrs ago.  
  • Mother – type 2 diabetes.  
- Medications (including OTC or shared medications):
  • Salbutamol inhaler – PRN; dose/route/frequency not documented.  
  • Dioralyte oral rehydration solution – recommended today; not yet started.  
  • Paracetamol – advised PRN for fever/weakness; dose/frequency not documented.  
- Immunisation status reviewed: Not recorded.  
- Sexual and reproductive health: Not recorded.  
- Physical activity and nutrition: Usual activity/diet not discussed; currently poor oral intake due to illness.  
- Alcohol, tobacco, and substance use:
  • Alcohol – infrequent/social.  
  • Tobacco – non-smoker.  
  • Other substances – not recorded.  
- Hearing loss or concerns: Not recorded.  
- Mood/mental health (including depression, self-harm risk): Not assessed; no concerns voiced.  
- Vision problems or recent changes: Not recorded.  
- Family and social relationships, caring responsibilities:
  • Lives alone.  
  • Works as a software engineer; off work last 3 days due to illness.

- BP, pulse rate and rhythm: Not recorded.

Investigations (as indicated)

- Fasting BGL and lipids (or random BGL if needed): Not ordered.  
- Cervical screening (if eligible and due): Not applicable (male).  
- STI screen (urine or swab – chlamydia/gonorrhoea if age 15–35): Not applicable (age 48; not discussed).  
- Mammogram (if eligible): Not applicable.  
- Other pathology (e.g., HbA1c, iron studies, Vitamin D): None ordered.  

Management Plan

- Diagnosis explained: Likely viral gastroenteritis.  
- Advice:
  • Maintain adequate hydration; use oral rehydration salts (Dioralyte).  
  • Paracetamol PRN for fever or weakness.  
  • Rest and remain off work until ≥24–48 h symptom-free.  
- Safety-netting: Return or book review if diarrhea persists beyond 5–7 days, worsening symptoms, blood in stool, or inability to keep fluids down.  
- Follow-up: Telehealth or in-person review next week if not improved.  
- Sick leave: Advised to continue time off work for next 1–2 days.  

Consider (not actioned during consult):
  • Routine preventive health review (BP, BMI, vaccines, alcohol/smoking screen, diabetes/cardiovascular risk given family history).  
  • CTG registration and allied health referral if chronic disease identified.

● Missing but clinically expected elements: BP, pulse, BMI, waist circumference, physical exam findings, urinalysis, immunisation review, mental health screening, routine bloods (BGL/lipids), alcohol use quantification, smoking pack-years (though non-smoker), hearing/vision assessment.  
● Internal contradictions: None identified.
